extra.message: Weak Session Token Generation Using Non-Cryptographic PRNG

metadata.proof: SESSIONID tokens are generated at line 202 using random.sample which relies on the Mersenne Twister PRNG (Python's random module) — not cryptographically secure. Although the token is 20 alphanumeric characters (62-char alphabet), Python's random module is predictable: an attacker who observes ~624 successive outputs can reconstruct the internal state and predict all future (and past) tokens. The secrets module (secrets.token_hex() or secrets.token_urlsafe()) should be used instead for session tokens.

extra.message: Broken SSL/TLS Configuration Re-enabling SSLv3 and TLS Compression

metadata.proof: When --ssl mode is active, lines 37-39 deliberately clear three secure default SSL context flags. Line 37 clears OP_NO_SSLv3, re-enabling the broken SSLv3 protocol (POODLE attack, CVE-2014-3566, allows plaintext recovery). Line 38 clears OP_NO_COMPRESSION, allowing TLS-level compression (enables CRIME/BREACH side-channel attacks on secrets in compressed HTTP bodies). Line 39 clears OP_CIPHER_SERVER_PREFERENCE, disabling cipher ordering which risks negotiation to weak export-grade ciphers.

extra.message: Session Confusion via Shared Class-Level SimpleCookie Across Threads

metadata.proof: The cookie object at line 141 is a class variable (VulnHTTPRequestHandler.cookie) shared across all instances in VulnHTTPServer (which extends ThreadingHTTPServer). A user without a Cookie header inherits session tokens set by another user's prior request on another thread, enabling session hijacking across users.

extra.message: Missing X-Content-Type-Options nosniff header

metadata.proof: The do_GET method sets Content-Security-Policy but does NOT set X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff anywhere. Without this header, browsers may perform MIME-type sniffing, potentially interpreting a resource served with content-type text/plain as text/html if it contains HTML content, lowering the bar for cross-site scripting vectors.

extra.message: Login form transmits credentials as URL query parameters via GET method

metadata.proof: The login form uses method="GET" instead of method="POST". On submission, the browser sends a GET request with credentials in the URL query string. This exposes credentials in server stdout logs (via self.requestline at handlers.py:159), browser history, Referer headers to third-party resources, web proxy logs, and the browser address bar visible to shoulder-surfing.

extra.message: Session tokens never expire allowing indefinite session hijacking

metadata.proof: The VulnHTTPServer creates an in-memory SQLite database with no session expiration logic. The session column stores tokens that are only updated (not invalidated) on login. There is no idle timeout check, no absolute session lifetime, no token rotation, and no server-side session cleanup anywhere in the codebase. Once a session token is stolen (SQLi at attacks.py:39, XSS at attacks.py:77/97, or logged via handlers.py:159) or fixated (attacks.py:231), it remains valid indefinitely.
